newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA OIL REFINERY OWES 371 BILLION LEVS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA OIL REFINERY OWES 371 BILLION LEVS.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim has debts worth 371 billion levs ($202 million) for last year and the first five months this year, the chairman of the parliamentary budget commission was quoted as saying.

Local media quoted Yordan Tsonev as telling reporters in the Black Sea port of Bourgas on Sunday that the refinery had posted a 33.4 billion lev loss in 1996 which had risen to 85 billion levs by May 30.
Bulgaria's new government which took office in May last month ordered an audit of the refinery. Tsonev said the audit results had been submitted to the chief prosecutor's office.
The audit showed that the refinery owed 168 billion levs in unpaid taxes by end May, and another 118 billion levs to oil suppliers for 1996 and the first five months of 1997.
Many of the losses were due to government-controlled prices failing to keep up with the lev's fall against the dollar. The government liberalised petrol prices in April.

A 1996 barter deal exchanging oil products for wheat has added a loss of 14 billion levs, Tsonev said, adding that Neftochim had bought 302,000 tonnes of wheat at $226 per tonne while the international market price then was $170 per tonne.

The refinery sponsored its Neftochimik football club with 364 million levs in 1996 and another 1.118 billion levs in the first five months of this year. The team qualified second in the first division soccer championship last season.
The plant built a modern football stadium in Bourgas at a cost of 1.913 billion levs.
Tsonev also mentioned salaries at the plant, which were significantly higher than the market average.
Bulgaria plans to offer up to 75 percent of the refinery for sale to private investors. Several firms including Russia's Rosneft have shown interest in the sale.
